primitive.relation: one contract, a chordless vertex-sequence cycle: a MathComp ucycle of host adjacency in which every host edge between two of its vertices joins cyclically consecutive entries (cyclic_chordless, over seq_cyclic_consecutiveb, no distinctness premise); three views differ only in the length bound. GTBase.induced_cycles.chordless_ucycle (no bound: the empty list and the two-vertex cycle of an edge qualify) is Extremal.D2str.induced_cycle by conversion (cyc_edge is seq_cyclic_consecutiveb); chordless_cycle (2 < size c, the same term as 3 <= size c) is GTMisc.X91.x91_induced_cycle (redundant u != v after the edge, Prop consecutiveness) and Packing.XE1.xe1_induced_cycle (redundant x != y before the edge, inline Boolean pair test) by explicit iffs; hole (3 < size c) is Chromatic.X3.x3_hole (three-way conjunction, u != v before the edge, Prop consecutiveness) and Minor.X27.x27_hole (x != y after the edge) by explicit iffs. The distinctness premises are proved redundant from sgraph irreflexivity (sg_edgeNeq), never added; no size, nonempty or uniqueness premise beyond each original is added, so D2str's sizes 0 and 2 stay raw-only. Since B24 a second, ordinal-map interface of the same module covers GTMisc.U13.induced_cycle and its existential wrapper GTMisc.U13.has_induced_cycle (normalized name has_induced_cycle), both by conversion: GTBase.induced_cycles.ordinal_induced_cycle f (f : 'I_k -> G injective, and f i -- f j exactly when i and j are consecutive modulo k in either order, equal indices included, ord_cycle_rel) and has_ordinal_induced_cycle G k. Order 0 is vacuous (every graph, the empty one included), order 1 is impossible in every sgraph, order 2 is an injectively enumerated edge, and for k >= 3 it is an injective chordless cyclic enumeration with its closing adjacency. It is not identified with the sequence views; its bridges to cycle_graph k and isubgraph are guarded by k != 1 (cycle_graph drops the diagonal, and cycle_graph 1 embeds in every nonempty graph). The three induced-isomorphism copies of cycle_graph n (Extremal.X49.x49_has_induced_cycle, Extremal.X60.x60_has_induced_cycle, GTMisc.X29.x29_has_induced_cycle) share the normalized name has_induced_cycle but are a different contract (an n-vertex set inducing a copy of cycle_graph n; order 1 admits a singleton): deferred-excluded, unchanged, not redirected. Distinct and untouched: X115's vertex-set odd induced cycles, X161's bare four-vertex ucycle, X169's clique-tree chordality (untouched at B23 and B24) and the directed chordal_C3; Packing.XE1.xe1_chordal was an unchanged chain of this family at B23. Since B25 both chordality presentations belong to family chordal (GTBase.chordal), and xe1_chordal unfolds to GTBase.chordal.chordal_by_cycles.

raw-unbounded.note: ucycle /\ every host edge between cycle vertices is a cycle edge, no length guard (sizes 0 and 2 included); D2str's peripheral cycle and the geodesic-cycle OPG row are frozen over it.

genuine-at-least-three.note: ucycle, 2 < size c (X91 writes 3 <= size c, the same term) and no chord; the redundant distinctness premise (after the edge in X91, before it in XE1) and X91's Prop consecutiveness are bridged by cyclic_chordless_prop_edge_neq / cyclic_chordless_neq_edge. X91's avoidable-path row and Erdos #81 (through the chain xe1_chordal, unchanged at B23; migrated by B25 to GTBase.chordal.chordal_by_cycles) are frozen over them.

hole-at-least-four.note: ucycle, 3 < size c and no chord; X3's three-way conjunction with u != v before the edge and Prop consecutiveness (cyclic_chordless_prop_neq_edge) and X27's x != y after the edge (cyclic_chordless_edge_neq). The X3 / X160 hole-length, constricting and rainbow rows and the X27 / X42 / X220 even-hole rows are frozen over them.

ordinal-map-modular-successor.note: U13's injective ordinal map with exact modular-successor adjacency (equal indices included) and its existential wrapper, aliases of ordinal_induced_cycle / has_ordinal_induced_cycle by conversion; order 0 vacuous, order 1 impossible, order 2 an edge. The current row two_colouring_a_graph_without_a_monochromatic_maximu_statement is frozen over them, and the complete C8+B24 Original freezes them with C8's raw splits_max_cliques / monochromatic chain.

induced-isomorphism-cycle-graph.verdict: distinct representation: an n-vertex set whose induced subgraph is isomorphic to cycle_graph n, not an ordinal map with exact successor adjacency
induced-isomorphism-cycle-graph.note: X49 and X60 (induced saturation) and X29 (normal graphs) keep their bodies and their A2 / A6 histories unchanged; at n = 1 a singleton qualifies there, unlike U13. Not redirected; a later task may relate them to has_ordinal_induced_cycle through has_ordinal_induced_cycleP, guarded by n != 1.

upstream_audit.note: MathComp path.v supplies ucycle (cycle && uniq, no lower bound) with rot_ucycle / rev_cycle / cycle_map; coq-graph-theory 0.9.7 has sgraph.ucycle_induced (a ucycle of an induced subgraph is a ucycle of the host) and the induced-subgraph / isomorphism machinery, but no chordless-cycle or hole predicate; GTBase.walks_paths supplies seq_cyclic_consecutive(b) with its reflection, rotation and reversal lemmas and the genuine seq_cycle. The three views are therefore new in GTBase.induced_cycles over ucycle and seq_cyclic_consecutiveb, related to seq_cycle by chordless_cycle_seq_cycle. B24: GraphTheory.core.digraph.isubgraph (F ⇀ G: an injective map with {mono f : x y / x -- y}) and GTBase.base.cycle_graph give the guarded bridges has_ordinal_induced_cycleP and ordinal_induced_cycle_cycP; cycle_graph's cyc_rel adds i != j and so differs from the raw modular-successor relation exactly at k = 1; no upstream ordinal induced-cycle predicate exists.

b24_review.scope: Ordinal U13 extension; original B23 review and source scope retained
